name: Asset Entities / Strive

snapshot.holdings: 26,355 BTC as of September 18, 2026 (up from 25,000 BTC reported the prior week)

email_summary: Strive bought another 1,355 BTC ($107.7M) to reach 26,355 BTC, funded partly by newly-active warrant exercises alongside SATA preferred sales.
bottom_line: Strive continued its weekly accumulation cadence, adding 1,355 BTC and diversifying financing with $21.2M of warrant-exercise proceeds alongside SATA preferred sales, which modestly eases reliance on dilutive preferred issuance. Continued share-count growth and an elevated market premium to Bitcoin NAV keep dilution and valuation-support risk as the key swing factors for the thesis.
source_conflicts: mNAV/premium figures vary by source and date: mnav.com cites 1.67x (as of ~21,356 BTC, three weeks old), an M1 summary cites 1.69x, and Yahoo Finance references a '90% NAV premium' tied to the 25,000 BTC disclosure — no single up-to-date mNAV figure could be confirmed for the 26,355 BTC holding as of Sept 18-21.

updates.headline: Strive buys 1,355 BTC for $107.7M, holdings hit 26,355
updates.what_happened: Strive disclosed via 8-K that it purchased 1,355 bitcoin between September 14 and September 18, 2026 at an average price of about $79,475 per coin, inclusive of fees, taking total holdings to 26,355 BTC. Class A common shares outstanding rose by 2,073,760 to 87,804,613 and cash grew to $229.6 million, a $25.4 million increase from September 11, while SATA preferred shares outstanding rose by 786,194 to 11,184,160.
updates.thesis_fit: Continues the core Bitcoin-accumulation narrative that underpins the treasury-wrapper thesis, but the accompanying rise in Class A shares outstanding is an ongoing dilution data point to track against Bitcoin-per-share growth.

updates.headline: Warrant exercises begin, add $21.2M, diversify funding mix
updates.what_happened: CEO Matt Cole disclosed that warrant exercises began during the week and generated $21.2 million in gross proceeds, with SATA preferred sales supplying the remainder of capital for the latest BTC purchase. Including the warrant proceeds, SATA accounted for 57.7% of total capital raised for the week, a lower share than in prior all-preferred weeks.
updates.thesis_fit: Warrant exercises give Strive a second capital-raising lever beyond the daily-paying 13% SATA preferred, which can reduce dependence on high-cost preferred dividends versus existing shareholders over time.
